boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Nevada-Reno, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daytime-to-evening first-weekend loop of campus orientation, public collections, outdoor landmarks and student-life resources.

cards.title: Start with Lounge
cards.subtitle: Find current student events and organizations
cards.notes: Log in with your NetID, browse the current event listings, and RSVP to one activity that fits your first-weekend schedule.
cards.short_summary: Use the campus engagement platform to turn an open weekend into a concrete plan.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Nevada, Reno identifies Lounge as its student-engagement platform for discovering events, connecting with organizations and getting involved.
cards.source_title: Lounge at University of Nevada, Reno
cards.access_notes: Current students begin using Lounge with their University NetID; incoming students can begin August 1.

cards.title: Orient at the Joe
cards.subtitle: Welcome Center on the first floor
cards.notes: Make the student union your early waypoint, then stop by the Welcome Center if you need campus-visit or Pack Pass guidance.
cards.short_summary: A central first stop with the Admissions Welcome Center on its first floor.
cards.evidence_claim: The University lists the Office of Admissions Welcome Center on the first floor of the Joe Crowley Student Union.
cards.access_notes: Check the student union and Welcome Center’s current service availability before making a special trip.

cards.title: Walk the Main Quad
cards.subtitle: North of Morrill Hall
cards.notes: Take a slow lap under the elm-lined lawn and use the walk to locate nearby academic buildings before your first week begins.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus landmark framed by 36 elms.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Arboretum says 36 elms line the Main Quad, which is just north of Morrill Hall.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus area; use established paths and observe posted construction or event notices.

cards.title: Find Morrill Hall
cards.subtitle: At the south end of the Old Quad
cards.notes: Pause at the exterior, read the building’s place in campus history, and use it as an anchor for navigating the Old Quad.
cards.short_summary: See the university’s first building, completed in 1885.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Nevada, Reno states that Morrill Hall, originally the Main Building, was the first building constructed at the University in 1885.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from public paths; building access may vary by campus operations.

cards.title: Circle Manzanita Lake
cards.subtitle: South end of the main campus
cards.notes: Follow the available path around the lake, take in the setting, and keep clear of active improvement areas and wildlife.
cards.short_summary: A central campus lake with ongoing accessibility and gathering-area improvements.
cards.evidence_claim: The University reports that Manzanita Lake’s pathways and gathering areas are being improved to make the landmark more accessible.
cards.access_notes: Follow posted detours and construction guidance around the lake.

cards.title: Take an Arboretum detour
cards.subtitle: Designated areas across campus
cards.notes: Choose one designated arboretum area and use the university’s materials to identify trees, shrubs, flowers, or native flora along the way.
cards.short_summary: Explore the campus’s state-designated living plant collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes the campus as a state arboretum with designated areas open to the public for enjoyment and educational pursuits.
cards.access_notes: Stay in designated public areas and leave plants and wildlife undisturbed.

cards.entity_name: John and Geraldine Lilley Museum of Art
cards.title: See the Lilley Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: University Foundation Arts Building
cards.notes: Check the exhibition schedule, then visit during listed public hours and leave food, drinks, flash photography, and tripods outside the galleries.
cards.short_summary: A campus art museum with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lilley Museum of Art is located in the University Foundation Arts Building, and its visitor page states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information | Lilley Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by season; the museum lists visitor guidelines and paid public parking options.

cards.title: Settle into the Knowledge Center
cards.subtitle: Library, technology, and study spaces
cards.notes: Walk through the main floors, find a comfortable study setting, and note the service desks and technology resources for your upcoming coursework.
cards.short_summary: A five-floor library hub combining study areas, collections, and technology support.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries describes the Knowledge Center as a five-floor building with collections, technology, experts, and study, classroom, and event spaces.
cards.access_notes: Visitors are welcome and everyone may enter and browse collections; verify branch hours before visiting.

cards.title: Look into natural history
cards.subtitle: Max Fleischmann Agriculture, room 300
cards.notes: Visit the lobby during the academic-term self-guided hours, then look for an upcoming public program or arrange a tour if you are visiting as a group.
cards.short_summary: Scientific specimens and displays connect visitors with northern Nevada’s natural heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Natural History says its lobby is open for self-guided tours Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., during spring and fall semesters.
cards.source_title: Education, Outreach and Tours | Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Self-guided lobby access is listed for spring and fall semesters only; confirm conditions outside those terms.

cards.title: Check out the Wiegand Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation and open gym
cards.notes: Review membership or guest-access requirements, then plan a low-key recreation session or ask staff about available drop-in classes and open-gym use.
cards.short_summary: Campus recreation space with courts and studios for movement-based activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the E. L. Wiegand Fitness Center has an open gym with three basketball/volleyball courts and studios for dance, yoga, and pilates.
cards.source_title: Working on campus | Employee resource center
cards.access_notes: Memberships provide facility access; confirm eligibility, fees, drop-in schedules, and guest policies with Fitness & Recreational Sports.
